I’m doing one final automated parity pass against the provided executable across a mixed set of success, help, abbreviation, and parser-error cases, so I can close with a concrete verification result rather than just spot checks.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc 'cases=(
  "--help"
  ""
  "--key a"
  "--val 1"
  "--key a --val x"
  "--key a --val 1 --foo 1"
  "--key b --val 3"
  "--key= --val 1"
  "--help=1"
  "--k a --v 1"
  "-ha"
  "--key a --val 1 -- extra"
)
status=0
for case in "${cases[@]}"; do
  py_out=$(mktemp)
  js_out=$(mktemp)
  set +e
  if [ -n "$case" ]; then
    /workspace/dataset/test6_executable $case >"$py_out" 2>&1
    py_code=$?
    node /output/test6.mjs $case >"$js_out" 2>&1
    js_code=$?
  else
    /workspace/dataset/test6_executable >"$py_out" 2>&1
    py_code=$?
    node /output/test6.mjs >"$js_out" 2>&1
    js_code=$?
  fi
  set -e
  if [ "$py_code" -ne "$js_code" ] || ! diff -u "$py_out" "$js_out" >/dev/null; then
    echo "MISMATCH: [$case]"
    echo "python_exit=$py_code node_exit=$js_code"
    diff -u "$py_out" "$js_out" || true
    status=1
  fi
done
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "All parity checks passed."
fi
exit "$status"'
